quickAnswer.title: Regular SIP projection
quickAnswer.question: What does the SIP Calculator model?
quickAnswer.answer: Use this page for a fixed monthly SIP where the contribution stays the same throughout the selected period. It estimates contribution, projected corpus and growth from your monthly amount, time horizon and assumed return.
quickAnswer.note: Market-linked returns are not guaranteed. This page models a regular SIP; use the Step-Up SIP Calculator when the monthly contribution increases over time.

links.label: Increase the SIP every year instead

contentSections.heading: Regular SIP vs step-up SIP vs lumpsum
contentSections.body: Use this calculator when you plan to invest the same amount each month. If you want to increase that amount every year, use the Step-Up SIP Calculator. For a single investment, use the Lumpsum Calculator.

faqs.question: Should I use this SIP calculator or the Step-Up SIP calculator?
faqs.answer: Use this calculator when the monthly contribution stays constant. Use the Step-Up SIP calculator when you want to model an annual increase in the contribution amount.

faqs.question: Is this the same as a lumpsum investment calculator?
faqs.answer: No. A SIP models repeated monthly contributions. A lumpsum calculator models a one-time investment compounded over a selected period.

quickAnswer.title: Annual SIP increase projection
quickAnswer.question: When should you use the Step-Up SIP Calculator?
quickAnswer.answer: Use this page when your SIP contribution is expected to increase periodically, such as after a salary hike. It is different from the regular SIP page, which keeps the monthly contribution unchanged.
quickAnswer.note: The result is an educational projection based on your contribution-growth and return assumptions, not a promised investment outcome.

links.label: Keep the monthly SIP fixed instead

contentSections.heading: What makes a step-up SIP different?
contentSections.body: A step-up SIP changes the contribution amount over time. That makes it useful for modelling a contribution plan that rises with income, while the regular SIP calculator is intentionally reserved for a fixed monthly amount.

faqs.question: Does a step-up SIP guarantee a larger corpus?
faqs.answer: No. Increasing contributions adds more invested money, but the final corpus still depends on actual market returns, timing and the assumptions entered.

faqs.question: Can I compare step-up SIP with a fixed SIP?
faqs.answer: Yes. Run the same horizon and return assumption in both calculators, then compare how the contribution schedule changes total contributions and the projected corpus.

quickAnswer.title: One-time investment projection
quickAnswer.question: What does the Lumpsum Calculator model?
quickAnswer.answer: Use this page for one investment made at the start and compounded for the selected period. It does not model monthly SIP contributions or annual SIP increases.
quickAnswer.note: The assumed return is a scenario input. Market-linked investment returns can be higher or lower and are not guaranteed.

links.label: Invest monthly with a regular SIP
Compare index and active-fund fee drag

contentSections.heading: Lumpsum is a one-time cash-flow calculation
contentSections.body: This page isolates the future value of a single starting investment. Use the SIP calculators for recurring contributions and the XIRR page when multiple investments entered at different times need an annualised-return estimate.

faqs.question: When is a lumpsum calculator more appropriate than a SIP calculator?
faqs.answer: Use it when the full amount is invested once at the beginning. A SIP calculator is designed for recurring monthly investments.

faqs.question: Can this calculator measure a portfolio with several purchase dates?
faqs.answer: No. For multiple cash flows made at different times, use the portfolio XIRR/annualised-return tool instead of treating them as one starting lumpsum.

index-fund-vs-active-fund-cost-calculato.targetKeyword: index fund vs active fund cost calculator india

quickAnswer.title: Fund cost-drag comparison
quickAnswer.question: What does this index-vs-active calculator compare?
quickAnswer.answer: It holds the assumed gross return constant and compares how different expense ratios affect future value. It is a fee-drag comparison, not a forecast that index or active funds will outperform.
quickAnswer.note: Actual fund performance, tracking difference, taxes, exit loads and portfolio choices can differ from this simplified cost comparison.

contentSections.heading: This page isolates expense-ratio drag
contentSections.body: The purpose is to answer a cost question, not a SIP-return question. Both fund routes use the same assumed gross return so the output shows the mathematical effect of recurring fund expenses over time.

faqs.question: Does a lower expense ratio guarantee better investment returns?
faqs.answer: No. The calculator deliberately keeps gross return equal to isolate fees. Real funds can have different holdings, tracking differences and performance.

faqs.question: Should I use this page to calculate my SIP corpus?
faqs.answer: Use the regular or Step-Up SIP calculator for contribution-based corpus projections. Use this page when the question is specifically the long-term cost difference between expense ratios.
